question: At an intersection where every approach is controlled by a STOP sign, what plaque is required and are plaques such as 2-WAY, 3-WAY, or 4-WAY permitted?
model_answer: Direct Answer: At an intersection where every approach is controlled by a STOP sign, an ALL-WAY (R1-3P) supplemental plaque must be mounted below each STOP sign, with a white legend and border on a red background. Plaques such as 2-WAY, 3-WAY, or 4-WAY are expressly prohibited with STOP signs. Standards (mandatory): - "At intersections where all approaches are controlled by STOP signs (see Section 2B.12), an ALL-WAY (R1-3P) supplemental plaque (see Figure 2B-1) shall be mounted below each STOP sign. The ALL-WAY plaque shall have a white legend and border on a red background." - "Supplemental plaques with legends such as 2-WAY, 3-WAY, 4-WAY, or other numbers of ways shall not be used with STOP signs." Guidance (recommended): - The TRAFFIC FROM LEFT (RIGHT) DOES NOT STOP (W4-4aP) plaque or ONCOMING TRAFFIC DOES NOT STOP (W4-4bP) plaque should be used at intersections where STOP signs control all but one approach, unless the only non-stopped approach is from a one-way street (this applies to not-all-way stop situations, not the all-way case). Options (permitted): - The CROSS TRAFFIC DOES NOT STOP (W4-4P) plaque may be used with a STOP sign when engineering judgment indicates conditions could cause road users to misinterpret the intersection as an all-way stop. - The W4-4aP or W4-4bP plaque may be used when such messages more accurately describe the traffic controls established at the intersection. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2B-1 shows the ALL-WAY (R1-3P) plaque with white legend on a red background alongside the STOP (R1-1) sign and related plaques. Citations: - Section 2B.04 Standard §4 (p.74) - Section 2B.04 Standard §5 (p.74) - Section 2B.04 Guidance §7 (p.74) - Section 2C.66 Guidance §3 (p.198) - Section 2C.66 Option §1 (p.198) - Section 2C.66 Option §2 (p.198) - Figure 2B-1 (p.74)
gold_answer: An ALL-WAY (R1-3P) plaque must be mounted below every STOP sign. Numeric-way plaques such as 2-WAY, 3-WAY, or 4-WAY are not permitted with STOP signs.
